evidence.description: acceptance_public.py::test_public_basic pins apply insert->[1], remove->[] on the default table
spec.md (353 lines) retains FR-001..FR-004 covering R01 with zero NEEDS CLARIFICATION markers

falsification_tests: apply([]) does not return []
apply with a non-dict op or op not insert/remove does not raise ValueError
remove contributes an entry to the returned list
claims.text: apply(operations) accepts a list of operation dicts (insert with dict document, or remove with positive-integer doc_id); returns inserted IDs in order, removes add nothing, empty input returns [], unknown/malformed operations raise ValueError.

evidence.description: acceptance_public.py::test_public_atomic pins ValueError and full rollback when a later remove targets missing id 99

falsification_tests: failing batch leaves partial inserts/removes visible
previously acquired table handle does not observe rollback
claims.text: Batch application is atomic: sequential validate/apply, on any error restore complete pre-batch default-table data; missing-ID remove is an error; previously acquired db.table('_default') handles reflect success and rollback.

falsification_tests: mutating caller's input dict after apply changes stored document
nested list in inserted doc shares identity with caller input
claims.text: Ordinary TinyDB reads/writes and preexisting documents keep working alongside the wrapper; inserted and returned nested data must not alias caller input; mutating an operation after apply cannot mutate the database.

evidence.description: acceptance_public.py::test_public_preview inserts an empty-dict document and expects success, pinning empty-dict acceptance

falsification_tests: apply remove with doc_id True does not raise ValueError
insert with non-dict document does not raise ValueError
empty-dict document is rejected
claims.text: Reject bool as doc_id despite bool being an int subclass; validate operations structurally before committing; raise ValueError for unsupported fields, non-list operations, or non-dict documents; accept empty dictionaries as documents.

evidence.description: acceptance_public.py::test_public_preview pins preview(ops)==[1] with len(db)==0, then apply(ops)==[1] (no ID consumption by preview)

falsification_tests: preview advances the next insertion ID
failed apply consumes IDs
after a batch with removes the next insert reuses or rewinds an ID
claims.text: preview(operations) returns the inserted IDs apply would produce while leaving all data and the next insertion ID unchanged, including on errors; preview and failed apply must not consume IDs; existing table handles and query caches stay coherent. Clarification: apply advances the wrapper's next-insertion-ID state on every successful batch and writes it back to the underlying table so subsequent inserts (apply or direct db.insert) continue the sequence without reuse or rewind, even across removes.

falsification_tests: two preview calls return the same list object
mutating an earlier preview result changes a later preview result
claims.text: preview must return a new, detached list on every call; mutating a previously returned preview list must not affect subsequent preview results or internal writer state.

falsification_tests: after db.insert({'x':1}) the next apply insert reuses id 1 or preview reports stale data
claims.text: Direct db.insert operations between wrapper calls must be seen by the wrapper; no stale initial snapshot may be cached.

evidence.description: acceptance_public.py::test_public_idempotent pins apply(ops, token='a') twice returning [1] with len(db)==1
spec.md now contains FR-015 (line 243) and User Story 4 (line 109) covering R07; 0 NEEDS CLARIFICATION markers

falsification_tests: second apply with same token+ops re-runs and duplicates the insert
token reused with different ops does not raise or silently changes data
failed batch with token blocks later reuse of that token
non-string or empty token is accepted
claims.text: apply(operations, token=None) supports an optional nonempty string idempotency token: repeating an already successful identical batch/token returns a detached copy of the original inserted IDs without rerunning mutations (even after other direct writes); reusing a token with different operations raises ValueError without changing data; failed batches do not consume a token; None means normal operation; invalid tokens raise ValueError.

evidence.description: spec.md now contains FR-016 (line 252) and SC-011 (line 307) covering R08; assumption A11 pins in-memory instance-scoped bookkeeping

falsification_tests: token state appears inside stored user documents
preview signature changes or records a token
mutating a returned list corrupts token bookkeeping
claims.text: Token bookkeeping belongs to the BatchWriter instance, never in user documents; preview never records/consumes a token and keeps its original signature; returned lists must not expose internal token bookkeeping through mutation.
